policy: Krea 2 Turbo may be used for private qualification only after the exact ComfyUI core/custom-node schema is verified in the live pinned runtime; production execution remains blocked until source, background, calibration, and independent-audit gates pass.

findings.finding: The primary Krea2EditModelPatch contract exposes VAE and source_image inputs for fit mode; the generated graph supplies both from the approved composite and Krea VAE.
The primary node documentation identifies 768 pixels as the grounded-encode default and describes a trained range beginning at 512; the generated graph locks grounding_px to 768.

The pinned ComfyUI revision 2a610155821d670a2d8047e654e5fce96b790eb5 exposes CLIPLoader with the krea2 type choice required by the primary Krea node contract. The live registry probe confirms the choice.

The pinned ComfyUI checkout and pinned comfyui-krea2edit checkout import on the local loopback server. All four API workflows match the live node registry, including Krea2EditModelPatch fit inputs, Krea2EditGroundedEncode inputs, and CLIPLoader type=krea2.

The required local qualification model files are present and SHA-256 verified by the model artifact preflight. This is an artifact inventory result, not proof that all weights can be resident or executed on the 16 GB Mac.

The live schema check passed, but no legally usable source fixture, approved background, calibrated thresholds, or independent audit evidence is present. Model loading and the required eight-step Turbo identity-edit execution were not attempted; production generation remains fail-closed.

conclusion: Krea live core/node/schema compatibility is verified in the pinned loopback runtime and all four workflows are live-schema loadable. This does not establish source-specific model execution or production suitability: the required eight-step run, identity/style experiment matrix, calibrated thresholds, and independent audit remain blocked by missing approved source/background and rights evidence.
